prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: boundary, dispatch, status; produces Export Limit Advisory when export capability<dispatch target; applies accepted export ceiling, records effective time. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes validated commands within protections, blocks conflicting commands, safe mode on auxiliary loss; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (alarms reviewed for export), Nacelle Condition Monitor feed Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): Leading Edge Tile Image, repeats pass if coverage insufficient; Blade Specialist reviews. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer (loading vs continuous/short-term limits), export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: authorized switching per approved instructions, clearances; on alarms limits switching, escalates; notifies Grid Dispatcher of export-affecting conditions; updates Shore Control Room. Electrical Technician works under isolation. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling, sheds loads, not for export unless approved; Start Test Trace; start failure→defect. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped data→Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); Session Revocation Receipt→Cybersecurity Gateway. Shore Control Room: dispatch target, ramp; on grid comms loss keeps last validated limit. Grid Dispatcher: targets/ramps; notified of material deviation/limit approach; priority safety>protection>export. Control Engineer validates, records deviation reasons. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): requested vs available, instruction/response history; Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint (scope, start, review). Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), crew vs schedule, dispatch constraints; Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master. Crew Transfer Vessel: Harness Audit Card. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record. Port Agent: Berth Slot Confirmation. Redoubt (permit control) blocks release until [truncated]. Vessel Master: confirms departure roster, reconciles headcount to manifest before underway; produces Crew Count Correction on mismatch. Personnel Tracking Console: accountability status. North/South Access Scanner record identity checks. Marine Coordinator: capacity/conditions, monitors transit;

New part:
S403: The Vessel Master records crew changes that occur during transit or between offshore locations.
S404: Personnel are accounted for before a transfer from a vessel to an offshore structure begins.
S405: Field Supervisor confirms the work party is complete before personnel enter the work area.
S406: Personnel report their arrival and departure at each active work location using the approved site process.
S407: Work access is limited to personnel whose assignment and authorization are current.
S408: HSE Officer verifies that personnel expected at the work site are accounted for during scheduled checks.
S409: The Vessel Master maintains an onboard count while personnel are aboard the vessel.
S410: Marine Coordinator reviews return movements so that shore personnel can anticipate vessel arrivals.
S411: Personnel are reconciled against the return roster when they disembark at shore.
S412: Field Supervisor escalates any unexplained absence or overdue check-in to Marine Coordinator without delay.
S413: When communications are unavailable, the responsible supervisor keeps a local record and reports it when service is restored.
S414: Accountability records retain the time, location, responsible role, and disposition of each material movement.
S415: Cybersecurity operations protect the wind farm control environment while supporting safe and reliable production.
S416: The Cybersecurity Gateway monitors traffic between operational networks and approved external connections.
S417: The SCADA Gateway records security-relevant access and control events for review.
S418: Monitoring rules identify unusual login patterns, unexpected configuration changes, and communications outside approved operating windows.
S419: The Cybersecurity Analyst reviews alerts, assesses their operational significance, and escalates urgent concerns to the on-duty operations lead.
S420: The Shore Control Room maintains an operational view of affected systems and coordinates immediate protective actions.
S421: Security monitoring is continuous, with alert coverage maintained during both routine operations and planned maintenance.
S422: Access is granted according to role, task need, and the current authorization of the individual or service account.
S423: The Control Engineer and SCADA Engineer use individually assigned accounts rather than shared credentials for interactive work.
S424: Privileged access is limited to approved personnel and is recorded for subsequent review.
S425: Access rights are reviewed at defined intervals and when a person changes duties or leaves the operation.
S426: Temporary access for maintenance is approved for a stated purpose and removed when the work is complete.
S427: Remote sessions require approved connection paths, strong authentication, and active supervision when they can affect live operations.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
